dedupe_keys.name: an improved daily standardized precipitation index dataset for mainland china from 1961 to 2018

description: An improved daily standardized precipitation index dataset for mainland China from 1961 to 2018 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Qianfeng Wang et al. The standardized precipitation index (SPI), one of the most commonly used drought indicators, is widely used in the research areas of drought analysis and drought prediction in different fields such as meteorology, agriculture, and hydrology. However, its main disadvantage is the relatively coarse time resolution of one month. Coverage: national (CN); published in 2022. Formats: CSV, Excel, TXT. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 1592894817 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
